examples.ko: 좋은 팀에는 지도력 있는 사람이 필요해요.
examples.en: A good team needs someone with leadership.
He has outstanding leadership, so everyone follows him.

examples.ko: 학급 회장은 지도력을 키우는 좋은 경험이에요.
examples.en: Being class president is a good experience for building leadership.
The boss earned the employees' trust through his leadership.
Leadership doesn't come just from speaking well.

examples.ko: 선수들은 새 감독의 지도력에 믿음이 있어요.
examples.en: The players trust the new coach's leadership.

explain: '리더십'이라고 더 자주 말해요. '지도력'은 신문이나 공식적인 글에서 많이 쓰고, '지도력이 있다/없다', '지도력을 발휘하다'로 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '리더십'이 더 가볍게 들려요.

phrases.en: He showed leadership in the crisis.
phrases.nuance_ko: 리더로서 가진 능력을 실제로 보여 줄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone actually shows their ability as a leader.

phrases.en: The new team leader still lacks leadership.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람들을 이끄는 힘이 약하다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say someone is weak at guiding people.

phrases.en: Our class president has leadership.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 뜻이에요. 일상 대화에서는 '지도력'보다 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning. More common than '지도력' in everyday talk.

explain_en: People often say 리더십 instead. 지도력 is used more in newspapers and formal writing, in forms like 지도력이 있다/없다 and 지도력을 발휘하다. In everyday talk, 리더십 sounds lighter.

examples.en: There are many students in the classroom who aspire to be writers.
My younger sibling is aiming to become a nurse.
He aspired to be an actor from childhood.
I'm happy I got into the department I applied for.
Which department are you going to apply to?
I came up to Seoul because I aspire to be a singer.

explain: 되고 싶은 직업이나 가고 싶은 학교·학과를 목표로 삼을 때 써요. 서류를 내는 '지원하다'보다 마음속 목표에 가까워요. '작가 지망생'처럼 명사 '지망생'으로도 자주 들려요.

phrases.en: I am an aspiring singer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 직업을 목표로 하는 사람을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a person aiming for a certain career.

phrases.en: The department I am aiming for is Korean Language Education.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가고 싶은 학과나 학교를 꾸며서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe the department or school one wants to enter.

phrases.en: I hope to become a doctor.
phrases.nuance_ko: '지망하다'보다 쉽고 넓게 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Easier and broader than '지망하다'.

explain_en: Use it when you set a job you want or a school or major you want to enter as your goal. It sits closer to a goal in your mind than '지원하다', which is handing in an application. The noun '지망생', as in '작가 지망생', is also very common.

en: letter of recommendation; letter of reference

examples.en: I asked my professor for the recommendation letter to submit to grad school.

examples.ko: 추천장 쓰는 데 시간이 오래 걸려요?
examples.en: Does writing a recommendation letter take a long time?

examples.ko: 선생님이 추천장에 제 장점을 자세히 써 주셨어요.
examples.en: My teacher described my strengths in detail in the recommendation letter.

examples.ko: 추천장은 다음 주 금요일까지 내야 해요.
examples.en: The recommendation letter has to be submitted by next Friday.
Please send the recommendation letter along with your résumé.
They say you can't apply without a recommendation letter.

explain: 입학이나 취업 때 다른 사람이 나를 소개하고 보증해 주는 글이에요. 한국에서는 '추천서'라고도 많이 말해요. 보통 '추천장을 쓰다/받다/내다'로 써요.

phrases.en: I asked my professor for a letter of recommendation.
phrases.nuance_ko: 추천장과 거의 같은 뜻이고, 일상에서는 추천서를 더 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Almost the same meaning as 추천장; 추천서 is more common in everyday speech.

phrases.en: My professor wrote me a letter of recommendation.
phrases.nuance_ko: 추천해 주는 사람이 주어일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the recommender is the subject.
phrases.en_equiv: to write a recommendation letter for someone

phrases.en: I submitted a letter of recommendation with my application.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지원하는 사람이 학교나 회사에 제출할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the applicant submits it to a school or company.

explain_en: It's a letter in which someone else vouches for you for admission or a job. In Korea people also say '추천서'. It's normally used as '추천장을 쓰다/받다/내다'.

en: to submit (a work) to an exhibition or contest

examples.en: I entered a painting in this contest.

examples.ko: 감독은 영화를 해외 영화제에 출품할 계획이에요.
examples.en: The director plans to enter the film in an overseas film festival.
Companies show their new products at the expo.
It is the day students submit their works.
After entering my photo, I wait for the result.

examples.ko: 어떤 작품을 출품할지 아직 못 정했어요.
examples.en: I haven't decided yet which work to enter.

explain: 영화제, 공모전, 전시회, 박람회에 작품이나 제품을 내놓을 때 써요. 목적어는 작품이고 장소 앞에는 '~에'를 붙여요. 그냥 서류를 내는 건 '제출하다'이고, 작품을 대회나 전시에 올릴 때가 '출품하다'예요.

phrases.en: The work I submitted won a prize.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자기가 대회나 전시에 낸 작품을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a work that you yourself entered.

phrases.en: I want to submit this painting to the exhibition.
phrases.nuance_ko: '~에' 앞에 전시회, 박람회 같은 행사가 와요.
phrases.nuance_en: An event such as an exhibition or expo comes before '에'.

phrases.en: I'm going to submit a new product to the expo.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞으로 낼 계획을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to talk about a plan to enter something.

explain_en: Use it when putting a work or product forward to a film festival, contest, exhibition, or expo. The object is the work, and the venue takes '~에'. Handing in plain paperwork is '제출하다'; putting a work into a contest or show is '출품하다'.

en: to obtain; to acquire (a license, qualification, right, property)

examples.en: I obtained my driver's license last year.
Getting a certificate helps with finding a job.
I have a friend who acquired Korean citizenship.
I'm going to graduate school to earn a degree.

examples.ko: 집을 취득할 때는 세금을 내야 해요.
examples.en: You have to pay tax when you acquire a house.
Please tell me how to earn credits.

explain: 자격증, 면허, 학위, 국적처럼 공식적으로 얻는 것에 써요. 말할 때는 '따다'가 편해서 '자격증을 따다'라고 많이 해요. 물건을 사는 건 '사다'예요.

phrases.en: I want to get a certificate this year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말할 때는 '취득하다'보다 '따다'가 훨씬 편해요.
phrases.nuance_en: In speech, 따다 is much more casual than 취득하다.

phrases.en: He obtained Korean citizenship.
phrases.nuance_ko: 국적처럼 공식적으로 얻는 것에 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for things you obtain officially, like citizenship.

phrases.en: To get a license, you have to take a test.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조건이나 목적을 말하는 연결형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A connected form that states a condition or goal.

explain_en: Used for officially gaining a certificate, license, degree or citizenship. In speech, '따다' is easier, as in '자격증을 따다'. For buying things, just use '사다'.

examples.en: The curator planned this exhibition.
I looked at the paintings while listening to the curator.
I want to be a curator working at a museum.
A curator selects and arranges the works.
A young curator is in charge of this exhibition.
I went to the art museum to interview the curator.

explain: 공식 직책 이름은 '학예사'(학예연구사)지만 일상에서는 '큐레이터'를 더 많이 써요. 관람객에게 작품을 설명해 주는 '도슨트'와는 달라요. 큐레이터는 전시를 기획하고 도슨트는 안내해요.

phrases.en: I met a curator who works at the museum.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공식 직책 이름이에요. 일상에서는 '큐레이터'를 더 많이 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The official job title; in everyday talk 큐레이터 is more common.

phrases.en: I want to become a curator someday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 장래 희망이나 직업을 말할 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when talking about future dreams or careers.

phrases.en: Curator, who painted this work?
phrases.nuance_ko: 직접 부르거나 높여 말할 때 '님'을 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add 님 to address someone politely or show respect.

explain_en: The official job title is '학예사' (학예연구사), but in daily life '큐레이터' is used more. A '도슨트' is different: a docent guides and explains works to visitors, while a curator plans the exhibition.

en: to master, to figure out (through practice)

examples.ko: 여러 번 실패한 끝에 요령을 터득했다.
examples.en: After failing many times, I finally got the knack of it.
I figured out how to ride a bike on my own.

examples.ko: 오래 일하면서 손님을 대하는 방법을 터득했어요.
examples.en: After working a long time, I figured out how to deal with customers.

examples.ko: 한국어로 말하는 요령은 자주 말해 보면서 터득했어요.
examples.en: I picked up the knack of speaking Korean by speaking it often.

examples.ko: 요리는 책보다 직접 해 보면서 터득하는 게 빨라요.
examples.en: With cooking, learning by doing is faster than learning from books.

explain: “터득하다”는 방법, 요령, 비결, 원리 같은 말과 잘 어울려요. 단어나 이름을 알게 됐을 때는 쓰지 않아요.

phrases.example: 일을 하면서 빨리 끝내는 요령을 터득했어요.
phrases.en: While working, I figured out the knack for finishing quickly.
phrases.nuance_ko: '터득하다'와 가장 잘 어울리는 짝말이에요. 해 보면서 알게 됐다는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most natural pairing with 터득하다, with the feeling of learning by doing.

phrases.example: 수영은 누가 가르쳐 주지 않아도 스스로 터득했어요.
phrases.en: I mastered swimming on my own without anyone teaching me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 남이 가르쳐 주지 않고 혼자 알게 됐을 때 '스스로'를 앞에 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put 스스로 before it when you learned something on your own without being taught.

phrases.example: 기계가 움직이는 원리를 터득하면 고치기 쉬워요.
phrases.en: Once you understand how the machine works, it's easy to fix.
phrases.nuance_ko: 경험을 통해 깊이 이해했을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when you have come to understand something deeply through experience.

dict_examples.en: To grasp the ways of nature.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 그는 일생을 걸려 배울 교훈을, 후방 근무 몇 달 만에 눈부신 속도로 재빨리 터득했다.
dict_examples.en: He quickly grasped, at a dazzling pace in just a few months of rear duty, a lesson that takes a lifetime to learn.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 길남의 어머니는 원래 시골로 떠돌면서 옷 보따리 장사를 했었는데 그러는 동안에 그 방면의 장삿속을 터득한 것 같았다.
dict_examples.en: Gilnam's mother used to wander the countryside selling clothes, and she seemed to have picked up the tricks of that trade.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: 터득하다 goes with words like method, knack, secret and principle. You would not use it for learning a word or a name.

en: to be outstanding; to be excellent

examples.ko: 그 학생은 수학에 특출한 재능이 있어요.
examples.en: That student has outstanding talent in math.

examples.ko: 동생은 노래 실력이 특출해서 상도 많이 받았어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling's singing is outstanding, so she has won many prizes.
He isn't outstanding, but he is a sincere person.

examples.ko: 그 선수는 어릴 때부터 달리기가 특출했어요.
examples.en: That athlete has been outstanding at running since childhood.

examples.ko: 특출한 능력이 없어도 열심히 하면 잘할 수 있어요.
examples.en: Even without outstanding ability, you can do well if you work hard.

examples.ko: 이 팀에는 특출한 선수가 한 명도 없는데 잘 이겨요.
examples.en: This team has no outstanding player at all, but it wins often.

explain: '뛰어나다'보다 다른 사람들 가운데서 눈에 띄게 잘한다는 느낌이 강하고, 조금 딱딱한 말이에요. '특출한 재능', '특출한 실력'처럼 명사 앞에 많이 쓰고, 반대로는 '평범하다'를 써요.

phrases.en: That athlete is outstanding at running.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서술형으로 쓸 때는 '무엇이 특출하다'처럼 잘하는 부분을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: As a predicate, it names what the person is outstanding at.

phrases.example: 제 성적은 특출하지 않지만 열심히 해요.
phrases.en: My grades aren't outstanding, but I work hard.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로 눈에 띄게 뛰어나지는 않다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form says someone isn't especially outstanding.

phrases.en: That student's singing is excellent.
phrases.nuance_ko: '특출하다'와 비슷하지만 더 부드럽고 일상 대화에서 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 특출하다 but softer and more common in everyday conversation.

explain_en: Compared with '뛰어나다', it stresses standing out clearly among other people, and sounds a little formal. It is often used before a noun, as in '특출한 재능' or '특출한 실력', and the opposite is '평범하다'.

examples.ko: 이 학교는 요리 특화 교육으로 유명해요.
examples.en: This school is famous for its cooking-specialized education.

examples.ko: 회사는 어린이 제품 특화 전략을 세웠어요.
examples.en: The company set a strategy to specialize in kids' products.

examples.ko: 이 앱은 여행 정보에 특화되어 있어요.
examples.en: This app is specialized in travel information.

examples.ko: 저희 가게는 매운 국수에 특화된 곳이에요.
examples.en: Our shop specializes in spicy noodles.

examples.ko: 지역 특화 산업을 키우는 일이 중요해요.
examples.en: Developing regional specialized industries is important.
You need a specialized skill to survive the competition.

explain: 한 분야에 집중해서 강하게 만든다는 느낌이라 '특화 서비스', '특화 전략'처럼 다른 말 앞에 붙여 써요. '전문'과 비슷하지만 '전문'은 사람이나 가게가 잘하는 분야를, '특화'는 제품이나 서비스를 그 방향으로 맞췄다는 느낌이 더 강해요.

phrases.example: 이 앱은 여행 특화 서비스를 제공해요.
phrases.en: This app offers a service specialized for travel.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한 분야에 맞춰 만든 서비스를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a service made for one particular field.

phrases.en: The bank released a product specialized for young people.
phrases.nuance_ko: 특정한 사람이나 목적에 집중한 상품을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A product focused on a specific group or purpose.

phrases.example: 이 병원은 암 치료에 특화돼 있어요.
phrases.en: This hospital specializes in cancer treatment.
phrases.nuance_ko: '특화'를 동사처럼 써서 어떤 분야에 강하다고 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses 특화 like a verb to say something is strong in one area.

explain_en: It carries the feel of focusing on one area to make it strong, and attaches before another word, as in 특화 서비스 and 특화 전략. Close to 전문, but 전문 is about what a person or shop is good at, while 특화 leans toward a product or service being tailored that way.

examples.en: The school accepted ten people.

examples.ko: 선생님이 학생들을 모두 합격시키고 싶어 해요.
examples.en: The teacher wants to get all the students to pass.

examples.ko: 회사는 올해 두 명만 합격시킬 거예요.
examples.en: The company will only admit two people this year.

examples.ko: 이 학원은 많은 학생을 합격시키는 것으로 유명해요.
examples.en: This academy is famous for getting many students to pass.

examples.ko: 시험 위원들이 그 학생을 합격시키기로 했어요.
examples.en: The exam committee decided to pass that student.
They gave good scores but still didn't pass them.

explain: '합격하다'는 시험을 보는 사람이 붙는 것이고, '합격시키다'는 학교, 회사, 선생님이 붙게 해 주는 쪽이에요. 시험 결과를 말할 때는 '합격하다'가 훨씬 많이 쓰여요. 반대말은 '불합격시키다', '떨어뜨리다'예요.

phrases.en: Please let me pass.
phrases.nuance_ko: 붙게 해 달라고 부탁할 때 쓰는 말이에요. 시험을 보는 사람은 '합격하다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to ask someone with the power to decide to let you pass. The test taker would say '합격하다'.

phrases.en: We will only admit ten people this time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 붙게 할 사람 수나 계획을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to talk about a plan or how many people will be passed.

phrases.en: The company did not pass that applicant.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기관이 붙여 주지 않았다는 뜻이고, 더 강하게는 '떨어뜨리다'라고 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means the institution did not pass the person. A stronger word is '떨어뜨리다'.

explain_en: 합격하다 is from the point of view of the test taker who passes, while 합격시키다 is from the side of the school, company or teacher who lets them pass. In everyday talk about results, 합격하다 is far more common. The opposite is 불합격시키다 or 떨어뜨리다.

examples.en: I want to work at a shipping company.
Korea is a country with a well-developed shipping industry.

examples.ko: 해운과 항공 중에 어느 쪽이 더 싸요?
examples.en: Which is cheaper, sea freight or air freight?

examples.ko: 해운업은 세계 경제와 깊이 연결돼 있어요.
examples.en: The shipping industry is deeply linked to the world economy.
My father worked in shipping for a long time.

examples.ko: 해운 운임이 크게 올랐다는 뉴스를 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw news that shipping rates rose sharply.

explain: '해운 회사', '해운업'처럼 산업이나 경제 뉴스에서 주로 써요. 하늘 길 '항공'과 짝으로 자주 비교돼요. 일상에서 배로 짐을 보낸다고 할 때는 '배편으로 보내다'가 더 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: My father works at a shipping company.
phrases.nuance_ko: 배로 짐을 나르는 일을 하는 회사를 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a company that transports goods by ship.

phrases.en: The shipping industry is greatly affected by the economy.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-업'이 붙어 산업 전체를 말해요. 뉴스에서 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: With -업 it means the whole industry, and it often appears in the news.

phrases.en: Shipping is well developed because there are many ports.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나라나 지역의 배 운송이 크게 성장했다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means a country's or region's sea transport has grown strong.

explain_en: Mostly used in industry and economic news, as in '해운 회사' and '해운업'. It is often compared with 항공 (air transport). In daily life, to say you send goods by ship, '배편으로 보내다' is more natural.

en: to win; to acquire; to obtain

examples.en: Our team won the gold medal.
In the game, your score goes up when you obtain an item.
It takes time to earn people's trust.
The goal is to gain a lot of support.
There's no way to obtain that information.

examples.ko: 점수를 획득한 사람만 다음 단계로 가요.
examples.en: Only those who earned points go to the next stage.

explain: '얻다'와 같은 뜻이지만, 노력해서 손에 넣은 결과에 쓰는 딱딱한 말이에요. 게임의 '아이템 획득', 경기의 '메달 획득'이 자주 보여요. 자격증이나 면허는 보통 '취득하다'를 써요.

phrases.example: 문제를 풀면 점수를 획득할 수 있어요.
phrases.en: You can earn points by solving problems.
phrases.nuance_ko: 게임이나 시험에서 점수를 얻을 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing used for earning points in games or tests.

phrases.en: I worked hard and got a good result.
phrases.nuance_ko: '획득하다'보다 쉽고 일상적인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier, everyday word compared with 획득하다.

phrases.example: 이 퀘스트를 끝내면 아이템을 획득할 수 있어요.
phrases.en: You can obtain an item when you finish this quest.
phrases.nuance_ko: 얻을 수 있다는 가능을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say that something can be obtained.

explain_en: It means about the same as '얻다', but it is a stiffer word for something gained through effort. You often see '아이템 획득' in games and '메달 획득' in sports. For certificates or licenses, '취득하다' is the usual verb.

dis.h: formal; gain a prize, right or result

p.n: 이기다 needs an opponent as its object, so a medal cannot be 'beaten'.
